title: An agent-based model to support community forest management and non-timber forest product harvesting in northern Thailand

key_points.claim: CoComForest ABM built for community forest management and NTFP harvesting in Nan Province, Thailand, used as a role-playing game and in participatory simulations.
key_points.evidence_quote: The model was used as a computer-based role-playing game to support sharing of perceptions and knowledge among stakeholders

key_points.claim: Implementation: UML conceptual model, implemented on the CORMAS platform.
key_points.evidence_quote: The Unified Modelling Language was used to build the conceptual model, subsequently implemented under the CORMAS

key_points.claim: Validation and participation: lab verification and calibration, then a workshop with 21 stakeholders, including co-validation.
key_points.evidence_quote: before using this tool with 21 diverse stakeholders during a field workshop

key_points.claim: Scenario results: outsider intensive harvesting accelerated resource depletion, while firebreaks increased resource availability.
key_points.evidence_quote: intensive harvesting practices of outsiders accelerated the depletion of resources, whereas the prevention of wildfire by establishing firebreaks could increase the resource availability

key_points.claim: Stakeholders found the model a useful common representation that facilitated communication on collective action.
key_points.evidence_quote: Most participants considered the model as a useful common representation of the system they manage collectively.

reliability_notes: Abstract only (from page metadata). Peer-reviewed open-access journal. It is a participatory/companion-modelling case study, not a general artificial-society paper.
